name: Classic Synthetic Optimization Test Functions
description: A family of classical artificial test functions used to benchmark continuous global-optimization algorithms, including Rastrigin, Ackley, Rosenbrock, Schwefel, Griewank, and Sphere. Each function has a known global optimum and exposes a specific difficulty: Sphere is unimodal and separable; Rastrigin, Ackley, Schwefel, and Griewank are highly multimodal; Rosenbrock has a narrow curved valley. They are evaluated across configurable dimensionality and serve as the standard sanity-and-stress testbed for evolutionary, swarm, and other metaheuristic optimizers.
evaluation_method: best objective value found / distance to known global optimum
general_score_metric: best function value / optimality gap at fixed budget
typical_sota_score: Algorithm- and dimension-dependent; strong metaheuristics reach near-zero error on low-dimensional Sphere/Griewank but struggle on high-dimensional Rastrigin/Schwefel.
reputation: The most widely used set of synthetic landscapes for testing global and metaheuristic optimizers; ubiquitous in evolutionary-computation papers and textbooks.
notes: Not an LLM benchmark; classical synthetic landscapes rather than a single curated dataset. No single canonical source; commonly aggregated in surveys (e.g., Jamil and Yang, 2013). Function definitions and global optima are standardized but parameterizations vary across papers.
